dimensions.label: Scope
dimensions.reason: The first three delivery phases and their deferred features are explicitly bounded.

dimensions.label: Risk
dimensions.reason: Provider-neutral startup injection and source-independent evidence are identified as the highest-risk boundaries.

dimensions.label: Effort
dimensions.reason: The work is separated into sequential foundation, recall, and optional-consolidation phases.

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.reason: Default behavior, scope rules, provenance, aging, and workflow ownership have been decided.

dimensions.label: Tests
dimensions.reason: Success criteria cover provider parity, startup recall, supersession, retries, isolation, and reliable misses.

problem: Wardian preserves provider continuity and agent-owned conversation archives, but neither is a provider-neutral long-term memory system. Agents cannot reliably begin a new provider session with the durable preferences, decisions, lessons, and current project state that should carry forward.

A useful memory system must make recall dependable before adding automated synthesis. It must remain local-first and inspectable, preserve evidence without duplicating conversation logs, avoid mandatory model quota usage, and keep memory scoped to the owning agent and active workspace.
goals: Make direct, evidence-backed memory saving and session-start recall available by default without an additional model call.
Deliver the same memory behavior across supported providers through Wardian-owned APIs and startup dispatch.
Keep automated consolidation optional, transparent, user-configurable, and implemented as a normal Wardian workflow.
Preserve durable provenance while allowing conversation archives and memories to follow independent retention lifecycles.
successCriteria: An agent can save, update, supersede, inspect, and remove agent-scoped memory through validated Wardian APIs.
Every saved memory contains normalized recall text, a durable evidence excerpt, an integrity hash, and zero or more optional source links.
Fresh provider sessions receive a bounded Stable memory and Current state brief before work begins; resumed sessions receive only the relevant delta since the last injected fingerprint.
Successful saves and startup loads appear as compact, expandable Memory saved and Memory loaded chat events.
Startup recall works when automated consolidation is disabled and consumes no separate provider quota.
Agent-wide memory and active-workspace memory are recalled without leaking another workspace's project state.
Stable memories persist until superseded or removed; current-state memories retain timestamps and become visibly stale rather than being silently deleted.
The consolidation workflow is off by default, uses a user-selected provider and model, resumes from durable archive cursors, and commits idempotently.
Regression tests prove provider parity, fresh and resumed startup behavior, supersession, agent isolation, stale-state labeling, retry idempotency, and reliable misses.

mvp.reason: A SQLite-backed authority, lifecycle API, scoping, provenance, and audit history are prerequisites for every recall path.
Useful memory must work without enabling a curator model or consuming separate provider quota.

full.reason: Session-start continuity is the primary user value and the most important reliability target.
Users need to inspect what was saved and exactly what context Wardian loaded.
Users may opt into automatic extraction and consolidation using their chosen provider and model.

outOfScope.item: Provider-native session history as durable memory
outOfScope.reason: Provider continuity remains a separate runtime concern.

outOfScope.item: Conversation archives as the memory source of truth
outOfScope.reason: Archives provide optional detailed provenance, while memory retains its own evidence excerpt.
Automatic consolidation is off by default and may consume the user's selected provider quota.

outOfScope.item: Memory-specific workflow reset, fork, compare, or restore controls
outOfScope.reason: The bundled consolidator follows the normal workflow sample lifecycle.

outOfScope.item: Automatic cascading deletion between conversations and memory
outOfScope.reason: The two stores have independent retention semantics.

future: Shared scopes with explicit cross-agent promotion policy.
Local semantic embeddings and reranking after startup recall is benchmarked.
Generic bundled-workflow upgrade controls, if introduced for all workflow samples.

phases.title: Memory foundation
phases.notes: Implement the SQLite authority, memory lifecycle API, scopes, evidence snapshots and source links, audit history, and direct-retention instruction contract.

phases.title: Reliable startup recall
phases.notes: Compile and inject bounded provider-neutral startup briefs, track fingerprints and resume deltas, and expose observable save/load events.

phases.title: Optional consolidation workflow
phases.notes: Add the ordinary bundled consolidation workflow, session-close invocation, curator selection, archive cursors, strict structured output, and idempotent memory commits.
